rootSeed.description: Sole source of true randomness for the entire run; everything else is derived deterministically from this via SeedTree.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, so an editor can attach it.

description: Top-level config for one full run — deserialized directly from the JSON file.
title: GlyphGen config

angles.description: Angles the arc may start (and end) at. Default Cardinal.

minSweep.description: Smallest sweep in degrees (a multiple of the preset's step: 90, or 45 for Both). 180 = a half circle. Default 90.

maxSweep.description: Largest sweep in degrees, below 360. Default 270.

ArcConfig.description: direction Arc: which part of the circle is drawn. The circle is set like a Circle rule's (its diameter runs from the current node to the node 'length' steps away); the arc starts at an angle of the preset, sweeps clockwise by a multiple of the preset's step, and so also ends on an angle of the preset.

crossing.description: Whether and where this shape's edges may cross edges already placed (curves count: a curved edge is checked as the curve it is drawn as). A crossing needs both shapes to accept it - the one being placed and the one that owns the edge it would cross - each by its own crossing settings.

spacing.description: Distances to keep from the shapes already placed (centroid and closest-node minimums/maximums). The rules of the shape being placed are checked against everything already there, so the outcome depends on placement order.

bias.description: Preference among placements that already satisfy every hard rule (grid bounds, crossing, spacing). Never relaxes a rule. Empty modes = no bias.

candidates.description: Shapes only: how many valid candidates to generate when a bias is active; the one whose glyph bounding box scores best is kept ("best of N"). Ignored without a bias, and by combination components (they search every placement exhaustively).

ArrangementRules.description: How a shape relates to the shapes already placed in the glyph: whether it may cross them, how far from them it must (or must not) sit, and which of several legal placements is preferred. Used by every entry in a language's shapes list and by the combination block (for the components of a composite).

width.description: Maximum stroke width (Taper/Ink) or nib length (BroadNib).

nibRoundness.description: 0 = a flat, square-ended nib; 1 = fully rounded ends (a capsule, like a brush pen). In between rounds the corners.

nibAngleWobble.description: How far (degrees, +-) the hand lets the nib angle drift along a stroke, slowly and seeded per stroke.

nibPressure.description: 0-1: how much the nib length (pressure) varies along a stroke.

nibLeadIn.description: 0-0.5: fraction of an open stroke's length, at each end, over which the nib eases in from a light touch to full length, like a hand setting the pen down and lifting it.

startBlobScale.description: >1 adds a blob where each stroke starts.

length.description: How many nodes the chain should have (including the start node).

connectionRules.description: Weighted connection rules driving the chain's growth at each step. At least one is required, otherwise no chain can grow.

connectionWeighting.description: How connection-rule weights turn into move probabilities. See ConnectionWeighting.

allowNodeRevisit.description: Whether the chain may revisit nodes already in it.

allowEdgeRevisit.description: Whether the chain may revisit edges already in it.

allowClosedLoop.description: Whether the chain may close into a loop back to its start node. How likely that is is set per rule (connectionRules[].backToStartChance).

selfSpacing.description: Node-to-node spacing rules inside this chain, all enforced together as each node is added, on top of the ordinary intersection check. Empty = none.

ChainRules.description: How ONE stroke (chain) grows: its length, the weighted connection rules, how those weights become probabilities, whether it may revisit nodes/edges or close into a loop, and the spacing between its own nodes. Used by every Generative shape - there is no language-wide copy, so two shapes can follow different rules (long strokes and short ticks, say) and nothing is inherited silently. Ignored for Literal shapes.

placements.description: Placement rules by component glyph ("*" = every component without a rule of its own). Components without a rule are placed as before.

CombinationArrangementRules.description: The arrangement of a combination's components: everything a shape's arrangement has, plus per-component placement rules. Placing order is the recipe's order, and each component is checked against those placed before it, so list the components you fix first.

modes.description: Empty = no bias: the first legal placement found is used (original behaviour).

weights.description: Optional weight per listed mode (default 1 for any mode not mentioned), e.g. { "Tallest": 3, "Squarest": 1 } to care three times as much about height as about squareness. A mode's score is multiplied by its weight before the scores are added; only the ratios matter. Weights for modes that aren't in Modes are rejected, as is giving every listed mode weight 0.

includeScaleAndRotation.description: Combination only (a shape's candidates are not scaled or rotated). false: bias only picks among TRANSLATIONS, at the first scale/rotation that has any legal placement (the existing "translate first, scale/rotate only as a fallback" order is kept). true: every allowed scale/rotation is also in the running, so e.g. Tallest can pick a larger scale or a 90-degree turn - strongest effect, but it overrides the translate-first preference.

CombinationBiasConfig.description: A preference, never a requirement: the bias only chooses between placements that already satisfy every other constraint (grid bounds, no crossing, sub-symbol spacing, allowed scales/rotations). If only one placement is legal, that one is used whatever it does to the shape. Components are placed one after another, so with three or more components the bias is applied greedily - each is placed to best serve the shape of what is already there. Several modes can be active at once; they are blended with equal weight (each is scored on a 0..1 scale relative to the grid, then the scores are added). E.g. Shortest + Narrowest asks for the smallest overall box, Tallest + Narrowest for tall and thin, Tallest + Widest for the biggest, Squarest + Shortest for a compact square. Opposites (Tallest + Shortest, Widest + Narrowest) cancel out and are rejected by validation.

recipes.description: Key = composite glyph name, value = component glyph names to overlay. A glyph name may appear both as a standalone entry in the language's glyph list and as a component here. Each value is a list of component names, or an object with "components" and an optional per-recipe "arrangement".

allowedScales.description: Discrete, lattice-validated factors only — see ScaleFactorConfig for why a continuous float range isn't safe here.

arrangement.description: How a composite's components relate to each other: crossing (default: none - overlay composition is controlled stacking, they may only touch at shared nodes), spacing bias and per-component placement rules (placements). A recipe can override parts of it with its own "arrangement". Each placed component counts as one shape. Components search every translation exhaustively, so arrangement.candidates does not apply here.

CombinationConfig.description: Overlay-composition rules for combined glyphs (e.g. Anchorite-style stacking). A composite glyph's components are generated independently first, then translated (and optionally scaled/rotated) onto the composite's own grid. On placement failure, the least-used dependency (via GlyphUsageTracker) is regenerated first, escalating through the recipe's components up to MaxRetriesPerRecipe before the run fails with a named error.

glyph.description: The component's glyph name. The rule applies wherever that glyph is a component of a recipe the arrangement covers (every instance, if a recipe lists it more than once).

sides.description: Prefer only: one or two sides. Two means a corner, so [Top, Left] is the top left. Left with Right, or Top with Bottom, cancel out and are rejected.

pick.description: SetRandom only: what is drawn. Default Any.

scope.description: SetRandom only: whether the draw is made once for the whole language (default) or again for every composite. See SetRandomScope.

offset.description: Fixed only: how far to move the component from where it sits in its own glyph, as { "x": 2, "y": 0 } or [2, 0]. Omitted = not moved at all (the plain overlay).

ifBlocked.description: Fixed only: what to do when the fixed position is blocked (crossing, spacing, off the grid). Default Regenerate, as before; Translate tries every other position first.

weight.description: Prefer and SetRandom: how strongly the side pull counts against the arrangement's bias, when both are active (default 1; 0 turns the pull off).

ComponentPlacementRule.description: Controls where one component (named by its glyph, or "*" for all of them) goes inside a composite.

minAngle.description: Smallest allowed turn, in degrees, measured between the previous edge and the new one at the current node: 180 = carry straight on, 90 = right angle, 0 = fold back. The first edge of a stroke has nothing to turn from, so it is not limited. Applies to every direction except Circle.

maxAngle.description: Largest allowed turn, in degrees (see MinAngle).

anglePreset.description: Shortcut for a minAngle/maxAngle pair; when set, it replaces them.

backToStartChance.description: Chance (0-100), each time this rule is the one picked, that the stroke instead goes back to its starting node and closes into a loop. Needs chain.allowClosedLoop and at least 3 nodes so far, and the closing edge must be free of crossings, otherwise the rule just makes its normal move. Replaces chain.closedLoopWeight.

arc.description: direction Arc only: which arcs may be drawn.

outlineNodes.description: direction Circle or Arc: extra nodes along the outline.

curve.description: How the edges this rule makes are bent when drawn.

ConnectionRuleConfig.description: One weighted connection template a chain can grow with: what direction, how far (in grid units, 1 = adjacent), how likely it is to be picked relative to the stroke's other templates, and how the edges it makes are drawn. A stroke with only one entry still works fine - it's just used 100% of the time since there's nothing to weigh it against.

baseGlyphsSheet.description: Also write a sheet of the language's base glyphs, as "_bases/_contact-sheet.png" (the main sheet never contains them). Only has an effect when baseGlyphs is used.

ContactSheetConfig.description: Settings for the contact sheet(s): one PNG laying a language's glyphs out in a grid.

axis.description: LongestStraight only: whether the mirror line runs perpendicular to the longest run (default), parallel to it, or either at random. With Parallel the copy lies beside the run, so it needs a gap of 1 or more to clear it.

toward.description: CenterWeight only: push the copy toward the middle (default) or toward the edge.

shapes.description: Ids of earlier shapes the rule looks at (all their instances in the glyph) instead of only the chain being copied. Longest straight run: the longest one among those shapes' strokes. CenterWeight: the average of all their nodes. Leave out (or empty) to look at the chain being copied alone. A listed shape that was not drawn adds nothing; if none was drawn, the chain being copied is used.

shape.description: Id of the shape to copy. It must be listed before this one.

flip.description: How the copy is turned over; see CopyFlip.

flips.description: Flip: Random only - the flips to draw from. Default: Horizontal, Vertical, Rotate180.

auto.description: Flip: Auto only - the rule that picks the flip.

gap.description: Steps the copy is moved away from the origin, along the direction it was flipped toward: 0 puts the copy's start on the anchor itself (the two share that node), 1 or more moves them apart, a negative number pushes the copy back over the origin so the two overlap or cross. Drawn from this range for each copy. Default 0 to 0.

shift.description: Steps the copy is slid sideways (across the gap direction), up or down at random. Drawn from this range, then given a random sign. Default 0 to 0.

anchor.description: Where the copy's start node goes before gap and shift.

preferNoCrossing.description: Try every flip position the config allows in random order and take one that crosses nothing already drawn. If none exists the best attempt is kept, but only when the destination's arrangement.crossing allows crossing (mode NodesOnly or Anywhere); otherwise the copy fails like any shape that cannot be placed. Turn off to take the first position that obeys the hard rules.

moveGlyphToFit.description: When no position keeps the copy on the grid (but one would, if the strokes already drawn sat somewhere else), the whole glyph so far is moved over, together with the copy, to where it fits. Turn off to fail instead. Not available to copies added by a derivation step, whose glyph keeps its source's position.

regenerateBase.description: First retry: when no position works for the copy, redraw the base shape (the first shape in this chain of copies that is not itself a copy) with fresh random numbers and try again, up to this many times. Everything placed after the base is rebuilt around the new draw. 0 turns it off. Only helps when the base is generated, not a literal.

redrawGlyph.description: Second retry, after the base redraws are spent: redraw the whole glyph from a fresh seed, up to this many times, before giving up with the error. 0 turns it off. Neither retry applies to copies added by a derivation step.

mirrorCurves.description: The copy's curves are the origin's curves, flipped with it, so the two look like mirror images. Turn off to give the copy curves of its own. (Copies added by a derivation step always draw their own curves.)

respectSelfSpacing.description: Apply the original shape's chain.selfSpacing rules between the copy and the original, as if the copy were more nodes of the same stroke: every node of the copy is measured against every node of the chain it copies (a node the two share is exempt, except in AllNodes mode). Existing and Adjacent both mean "every node of the original" here. The copy's own nodes need no check, a flip keeps their distances. Default false.

selfSpacingIgnoresOriginal.description: With respectSelfSpacing: for Existing and AllNodes rules, leave the original chain out and measure the copy against every OTHER node already in the glyph instead (the original's own nodes do not count, so the copy may sit as close to it as arrangement allows). Adjacent rules still compare with the original. Default false.

CopyConfig.description: Turns a shape into a copy of another shape (put it on the destination entry in the shapes list; the origin entry must come earlier in the list). Instead of being drawn, the destination becomes one copy of every instance of the origin, flipped around the origin chain's start node and then moved by the anchor, gap and shift. A copy can itself be copied. The destination takes no chain, nodes, placement or count of its own; its arrangement (crossing, spacing, bias) decides which copy positions are acceptable.

nodeTolerance.description: NodesOnly: how far (lattice units) from a node a crossing may lie and still count as being at it. A stroke passing near a node but not through it is fine. Default 0.3.

nodesOfShapes.description: NodesOnly: only the nodes of these shapes (ids) count. Empty/missing = every node (the shape's own included). With a list, the shape's own nodes count only if its own id is listed.

CrossingConfig.description: Crossing rules of one shape (arrangement.crossing). Curves are taken into account.

edge.description: Curve settings for edges that no connection rule made (the edges of Literal shapes).

forceAllEdgesCurved.description: Plans EVERY edge as a curve: ignores every chanceToBeCurved and the proximity guard (both would otherwise force edges straight), so "curved" really means curved everywhere. Whether an edge visibly bends still depends on tension: a 0..0 tension band gives a bezier that looks straight. Must not be combined with a chanceToBeCurved below 100 or an enabled guard (the loader rejects that, since they would be silently overridden). Default false.

CurveConfig.description: Rendering-time curve behavior that is NOT per edge. How an edge bends (chance, mode, tension, jitter) is set on the connection rule that made it - see EdgeCurveConfig. Kept independent of the underlying straight-edge grid topology (which is what intersection checks always operate on): this only affects how the final glyph is drawn, never whether a connection is valid.

minEdgeLength.description: Edges shorter than this (grid units) are always forced straight - a curve on a very short edge exaggerates its bulge relative to the edge's own length, making it more likely to swing into nearby geometry.

CurveProximityGuardConfig.description: Forces an edge straight based on geometry, independent of the edge's curve settings - a safety net against a curve bulging into nearby ink (see CurvePlanner's remarks on this). Disabled by default since it changes how many edges end up curved vs. the language's other settings alone would produce.

percent.description: Percentage (0-100) of all nodes (node steps) or all edges (edge steps) that exist when the step runs, rounded to a whole number. Resolved uniformly in the range.

count.description: A fixed number of nodes/edges, drawn uniformly (inclusive) from the range.

DerivationAmount.description: How much a step affects: a percentage of what exists, or a fixed number, each as a range. Set exactly one of Percent and Count.

DerivationCondition.description: A gate on a step: it only runs when the glyph, as it is when the step comes up (after the earlier steps), has a number of edges and nodes within these limits. Every limit that is set must hold; none set = no gate. Nodes are the distinct points, including lone ones; a circle or dot is one edge.

finalOutputRotation.description: When the derived glyph is drawn at its source's render.rotateOptions angle instead of drawing its own. Only steps that actually ran count (one skipped by chance or onlyIf does not).

from.description: The glyph (a name from glyphs or baseGlyphs; plain, composite or itself derived) to start from.

maxSimilarityToSource.description: Quality gate against the source only: the derived glyph may resemble it by at most this much (0-1, same measure as quality.maxSimilarity), so it can't be a copy. 1 turns it off. Against every OTHER glyph the normal quality.maxSimilarity applies. Default 0.9.

DerivationConfig.description: A glyph made from another glyph: the source is generated first, then the steps edit a copy of its strokes (a composite source is flattened to plain strokes). The source itself is left as it was. Edges that survive untouched keep the source's exact curves.

onlyIf.description: Only run the step if the glyph has enough / not too many edges and nodes at that point (see DerivationCondition). Checked before chance. A skipped step changes nothing and uses no random numbers.

chance.description: Chance (0-100) that the step runs at all. Default 100.

amount.description: DeleteNodes, DeleteEdges, Keep, Nudge: how many. For Keep it is how many edges stay.

target.description: DeleteNodes, Nudge: which nodes may be picked. Default Any.

connectionRules.description: DeleteNodes with Mode Bridge: the moves a replacement path may be built from. Same options as chain.connectionRules (Circle rules are ignored).

bridgeMaxMoves.description: DeleteNodes with Mode Bridge: most moves a replacement path may have. Default 3.

removeOrphanNodes.description: DeleteNodes, DeleteEdges, Keep: also remove nodes left with no edge. Default true. If false they stay as lone nodes (invisible when drawn, but they still count as nodes for later steps, for similarity, and in the debug view).

keepAtLeast.description: DeleteNodes, DeleteEdges, Keep: never end with fewer edges than this (picks that would are skipped). Default 1.

keepConnected.description: DeleteNodes, DeleteEdges, Keep: skip any pick that would split the glyph into more connected pieces than it had before the step. Default false.

shapes.description: Add: ids of entries of the language's shapes, each placed as it would be in a plain glyph (its count, chain, placement and arrangement), against the strokes that are left. Added strokes may cross the existing ones only if the shape's arrangement.crossing says so.

optional.description: Add: if a shape cannot be placed, skip it instead of failing. Default false.

factors.description: Scale: weighted ratios, one is picked. A ratio that would not fit the grid is not picked.

degrees.description: Rotate: the allowed rotations (90, 180, 270); one is picked. Default all three.

distance.description: Nudge: how far a node may move on each axis. Default 1.

DerivationStep.description: One step of a derivation. A single class for every op, so only the options that belong to the op are allowed (the loader rejects the others).

chanceToBeCurved.description: Chance (0-100) that an edge made by this rule is drawn as a curve; otherwise it is a straight line. Rolled per edge. Default 0 = every edge straight; 100 = always curved (a 0..0 tension still looks straight). This replaces the old language-wide straightLineBias (chanceToBeCurved = 100 - straightLineBias).

mode.description: How the edge's end tangents are chosen. Derived: from the neighbouring nodes (smooth spline feel). Explicit: each end gets its own randomized tangent. Hybrid: Derived or Explicit per edge, at random.

tension.description: Bezier handle length as a fraction of the edge length; each handle draws its own value.

explicitJitterDegrees.description: Explicit/Hybrid: max angle (degrees) an end tangent may deviate from the derived one.

EdgeCurveConfig.description: How ONE edge is bent when drawn. Each connection rule carries its own copy, so a rule can make long edges gentle curves and short ticks dead straight within the same stroke. Edges that come from no rule (Literal shapes) use curve.edge instead. Only affects drawing - never whether a connection is valid.

FloatRange.description: A plain floating-point range (no percent semantics), resolved the same way as IntRange/PercentRange. Used for render settings expressed as canvas fractions, degrees, tension, etc.

IntRange.description: An inclusive integer range, resolved to one concrete value per generation via the deterministic per-glyph random source (so re-running the same config+seed always resolves to the same value).

angle.description: Degrees, 0 to 180, inclusive at both ends.

outer.description: Replacement outer join, or omitted to keep the context's.

inner.description: Replacement inner join, or omitted to keep the context's.

JoinAngleRule.description: Replaces the outer and/or inner join for nodes whose angle falls in a range.

outer.description: The convex outside of the bend.

inner.description: The notch between two strokes. Overlap (the default) leaves it as it is.

byAngle.description: Overrides for particular angles, tried in order; the first rule whose angle range contains the angle wins, and whatever it leaves out falls back to outer / inner above. The angle is the one between the two strokes: 180 = straight on, 90 = a right angle, 45 = a sharp turn. On the grid that is almost always 45, 90 or 135; on curves it varies.

JoinContextConfig.description: The outer and inner join for one kind of node, plus optional per-angle overrides.

miterLimit.description: Outer Miter only: beyond this point-length / half-width ratio a miter falls back to a bevel.

size.description: Inner Bevel / Round only: chamfer length or fillet radius, in half-widths of the stroke (1 = as large as half the stroke width). Limited automatically so it never reaches past the neighbouring node.

axis.description: Outer Level only: the line the corner is cut along. Auto = across the corner's outward direction, so a V pointing down is cut flat on the bottom and a corner pointing right is cut along its column.

JoinSideConfig.description: One side (outer or inner) of a join.

JoinsConfig.description: How strokes are joined, for every typeface. A "corner" is a bend within one stroke; a "junction" is any node where strokes meet (tip to tip, a tip on another stroke, a crossing, a stroke revisiting its own node). Each has an OUTER side (the convex outside of the bend, where ink is added to make a point or round) and an INNER side (the notch between two strokes, which can be filled with a chamfer or fillet).

trimCaps.description: If true, tips that end at a junction (a node where another stroke is also present) are drawn without their caps, Ball terminals or start blobs, and the joins above fill the node instead. A tip that stands alone keeps all of them. With outer Overlap nothing fills the node, so pair this with Miter, Bevel or Round.

straightenInnerDegrees.description: 0 = off. Where two strokes meet within this many degrees of straight (180) and the NOTCH between them (the side that bends inwards, under 180 degrees) has no other stroke in it, that notch is filled with a long chamfer (see straightenLength) so the edge reads as one straight line instead of a kink. Other strokes may leave the node on the other side. Replaces the inner join for those notches.

straightenOuterDegrees.description: 0 = off. The same for the OUTSIDE of the bend (the side that bends outwards, over 180 degrees), e.g. the top of a T whose bar is slightly bent that way. Ink cannot be removed, so instead the edges are extended along one straight line through the corner and the thin wedges between that line and the real edges are filled; each wedge ends in a small step whose height grows with the angle and with straightenLength. Replaces the outer join for those gaps.

straightenLength.description: Length of the straightening fill along each stroke's edge, in half-widths. Limited automatically so it never reaches past the neighbouring node.

JunctionJoinConfig.description: The join settings for strokes meeting at a node: everything a corner has, plus how the tips that end there are treated.

grid.description: The lattice this language's glyphs are drawn on. Required per language.

items.description: A glyph name, e.g. "warrior" (the older { "name": "warrior" } form also loads).

glyphs.description: The language's real glyphs - these end up in the output atlas/contact sheet.

items.description: A glyph name, e.g. "warrior" (the older { "name": "warrior" } form also loads).

baseGlyphs.description: Glyphs that exist only to be components of combination recipes. Generated (before Glyphs, so recipes can use them) and rendered, but written to a separate "_bases" folder and left out of the contact sheet. They go through the same quality/similarity gate as every other glyph.

usageSizeBias.description: Glyphs used in more recipes roll lower counts/lengths, for shapes that have a count (guaranteed shapes are unaffected).

shapes.description: What every plain (non-composite) glyph is built from, placed in list order: each entry carries its own chain rules, placement and arrangement. A guaranteed motif is an entry without a count; free-form strokes are entries with one.

derivations.description: Glyphs made by editing another glyph, by glyph name. A name listed here is not generated from shapes and has no recipe. See DerivationConfig.

quality.description: Post-generation gates (similarity to other glyphs, straight-line rejection).

render.description: Rendering (framing, colours, typeface). Pixel size/margin come from Canvas.

angles.description: AtAngles: which angles get a node. Default Cardinal.

snap.description: AtAngles: how a point between lattice points is handled. Default Within.

tolerance.description: How close (lattice units) the outline must pass to a lattice point for Within and EveryLatticePoint. Default 0.3.

OutlineNodesConfig.description: Extra nodes along a circle or arc (on a connection rule with direction Circle or Arc). They count as nodes of the shape for spacing, startOnExistingNode and NodesOnly crossings; the chain itself still continues from the far node.

PercentRange.description: A percentage hint (0-100), resolved the same way as IntRange. Used as a soft bias (e.g. StraightLineBias), not a hard constraint.

PlacementBounds.description: An inclusive box of lattice node coordinates (placement.bounds).

oneOf.description: One origin, or an array of origins from which one is picked at random.

fixedOrigin.description: Required when Mode == Fixed, and an error with any other mode (it would be ignored). Written as { "x": 7, "y": 9 } or [7, 9] - or as an array of such points, in which case one is picked at random for each glyph (a failed try moves on to the next of a shuffled order, so every origin is tried before giving up).

discardUsedOrigins.description: Fixed with several fixedOrigin points: an origin an earlier instance of this shape (same glyph) was placed at is not used again, so a shape with count N and N origins fills each of them once. When every origin is used the instance cannot be placed. Default false.

bounds.description: A box smaller than the grid that this shape must stay inside, treated as the edge of the grid while the shape is generated and placed (nodes, and circles' whole outlines). Inclusive node coordinates, e.g. { "minX": 4, "minY": 4, "maxX": 10, "maxY": 10 }. Other shapes are not limited by it. null = the whole grid.

allowRotationOnPlace.description: Allows a random rotation per attempt, from Rotations (below). Only Literal motifs are affected: a generated chain is already random and ignores the rotation.

rotations.description: The angles (0/90/180/270) this placement may rotate by - meaningful only for a Literal motif's placement; the loader rejects it anywhere else. null (default) = inherit Combination.Rotation when Combination.AllowRotate is on, which is the original coupling; a list = use exactly these; an empty list = never rotate.

maxPlacementAttempts.description: Failure budget for "find/fit a shape at a location" — distinct from CombinationConfig.MaxRetriesPerRecipe, which governs "can this recipe's components work together at all". Keeping these separate lets failure messages say precisely which stage gave up.

redoShape.description: When an instance of this shape cannot be placed within maxPlacementAttempts: how many times to redraw ALL instances of this shape (new chains, new positions) before giving up on this try of the glyph. Earlier shapes stay as they are. Default 0 = no redraw (the glyph fails, as before).

redrawGlyph.description: After redoShape is spent: how many times to redraw the WHOLE glyph from a fresh seed (every shape again) before the failure is reported. Default 0.

startOnExistingNode.description: RandomValid only: start the shape on a node already in the glyph (chosen uniformly) instead of a random grid point, so shapes grow out of each other. Needs no crossing permission - edges that merely meet at a node don't count as crossing - but can't be combined with SubSymbolSpacing.MinNodeDistance > 0 (a shared node is distance 0).

startOnExistingNodeChance.description: With startOnExistingNode: the chance (0-100) that an attempt starts on an existing node; otherwise it starts on a random grid point as usual. Rolled per attempt. Default 100 = always start on a node.

startOnShapes.description: With startOnExistingNode: only the nodes of these shapes (ids of EARLIER shapes) count as places to start on. null (default) = every node already in the glyph. When none of the listed shapes was drawn in this glyph, there is nothing to attach to and the shape is placed like the first one, at a random point.

side.description: RandomValid only: pull the shape towards a side or corner of the glyph. null = no pull. It ranks the shape's best-of-N candidates (arrangement.candidates), so raise that for a stronger pull.

PlacementConfig.description: One shared schema for "where does this shape go" — used identically by both guaranteedMotifs[].placement and a language's subSymbolPlacement, so there's a single validator and a single resolver implementation for both cases.

maxSimilarity.description: Jaccard similarity (0-1) of two glyphs' normalized shapes, at or above which they're considered too similar and one gets regenerated. 1.0 (or higher) disables the check entirely. Default 0.7 matches "no more than 70% alike".

rejectStraightLineOnly.description: Reject a glyph whose entire geometry (across all its chains/components) reduces to a single straight line with no bends.

compositeMaxSimilarity.description: Similarity limit for COMPOSITES, checked only against other composites - never against plain or base glyphs, which a composite contains by construction. 1.0 or more (the default) = composites are not compared at all, as before. A composite at or above the limit is rebuilt with a fresh seed, up to MaxRegenerationAttempts. Composites are never subject to RejectStraightLineOnly.

QualityConfig.description: Post-generation quality gates applied to every finished glyph in a language, checked against every glyph already accepted earlier in the same run. A glyph failing either check is regenerated (fresh seed) up to MaxRegenerationAttempts times before the run fails with a clear error naming the glyph.

capLevel.description: With cap Level: which line the end is cut along. Horizontal = flat on the node's row (like text on a baseline), Vertical = along its column, Auto = across the stroke's dominant direction, so a stroke steeper than 45 degrees is cut horizontally and a flatter one vertically. Straight horizontal and vertical strokes are never changed.

capLevelFlat.description: With cap Level: what happens to an end that is already flat on the axis. ExtendToNeighbours grows every end to half a stroke width past its node's row (or column), so verticals, horizontals and diagonals all stop on one line.

RectangularTypefaceConfig.description: Constant-width strokes. Independent of curve.mode: on a curved edge you simply get a constant-width band following the curve. All widths in this file's configs are fractions of the canvas size, so stroke weight looks the same at any pixel size and in any framing mode.

rotateDegrees.description: Turns every glyph by this many degrees, clockwise, around the middle of its grid; the canvas itself stays as it is. Any angle works (curves turn exactly). The framing then fits the turned glyphs, so with Grid framing the grid's square is what is rotated and its corners may reach past the canvas margin. Applies to the normal and the debug images alike. Default 0.

rotateOptions.description: Per-glyph random turn, added to rotateDegrees: each glyph draws one option by weight, then an angle uniformly from that option's range (degrees, clockwise). The draw comes from the glyph's own seed, so a glyph always turns the same way. Empty (default) = no random turn. Example: [ { "min": -8, "max": 8, "weight": 4 }, { "min": 85, "max": 95, "weight": 1 } ] mostly tilts a little and now and then lays a glyph on its side.

background.description: #RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB; the default is fully transparent.

joins.description: How strokes are joined where they bend and where they meet, for every typeface.

contactSheet.description: The overview sheet(s) the CLI writes next to the glyph images.

debugShowNodes.description: Debug option. When any of the debug options is on, the CLI writes an extra "<glyph>.debug.png" next to each normal image, drawn with the enabled overlays (the normal images stay clean; with all of them off no debug files are written). Overlay for checking generation output: the whole lattice as faint dots with coordinates labelled every 5 cells, plus a dot on every node of the glyph - red for a free-form sub-symbol, blue for a guaranteed motif, gold where a node is used more than once (a revisit, or a node shared by shapes).

debugColorComponents.description: Debug option (see DebugShowNodes): colour each combination component differently in the extra ".debug.png" images.

debugColorParts.description: Debug option (see DebugShowNodes): in the extra ".debug.png" images, colour the ink each kind of part ADDS on top of the stroke bodies - grey for caps (and Ball / Ink terminals), violet for corner joins, pink for junction joins (including straightening). The strokes themselves keep the foreground colour (or their component colour). Parts are painted over the strokes in the order they are built: corner joins, then junction joins, then caps.

debugColorShapes.description: Debug option (see DebugShowNodes): in the extra ".debug.png" images, give every shape its own colour, in the order of the shapes list. Instances of one shape (a shape with a count, or a copy of each instance) share its hue and differ in lightness, so they can be told apart. Joins between strokes keep the foreground colour. Takes the place of debugColorComponents where both are on.

debugShowUndrawn.description: Debug option (see DebugShowNodes): in the extra ".debug.png" images, also draw the shapes that have isDrawn = false, in one translucent orange. They are never in the normal images.

RenderConfig.description: Per-language rendering settings. Pixel size and margin still come from CanvasConfig.

min.description: Smallest angle in degrees (clockwise; negative turns the other way).

weight.description: Relative chance of this option (default 1; 0 = never).

RotateOption.description: One weighted range of turns for render.rotateOptions.

weight.description: One weight shared by every non-zero angle (there are no per-angle weights): how likely a rotated placement is, relative to an unrotated one (weight 1), when the combination search falls back to trying scale/rotation combinations. 1 = rotated as likely as not, 0.5 = half as likely, 0 = never rotate. Multiplies with the scale factor's weight.

RotationConfig.description: Allowed rotation angles for overlay composition. Only 0, 90, 180 and 270 are supported (they keep every node on the grid; GridPoint.RotateAround throws for anything else, 45 included) - the config loader rejects other angles.

ScaleFactorConfig.description: One allowed scale factor for overlay composition, expressed as an exact fraction rather than a float — necessary because lattice-safety of shrinking depends on exact divisibility of every node's offset from the component's anchor, which a float range can't express or validate cleanly. The per-component check lives in CombinationResolver.IsLatticeSafeScale: a shrinking factor is only usable if every node's coordinates divide exactly for the specific shape being scaled, so "nicer" geometry (lots of even-length edges) naturally shrinks more often than oddly shaped components, without the generator having to force it. Weight orders the fallback search: heavier factors are tried earlier (it multiplies with Rotation.Weight for a rotated placement); 0 = never use this factor. With every weight equal the order is a plain uniform shuffle.

lookback.description: Adjacent mode only: how many of the chain's most recent nodes are checked.

SelfSpacingRule.description: One node-to-node spacing rule applied while a single chain grows. Several rules (even of the same Mode) can be active at once; a new node must satisfy all of them. Distances are in grid units, 0 = that bound is off.

id.description: Unique within the language. Names the shape in error messages and seeds its random streams, so renaming it changes the glyphs.

count.description: How many instances per glyph, rolled once per glyph. Omit for exactly one guaranteed instance (no roll).

chance.description: Chance (0-100) that this entry is drawn in a glyph at all, rolled once per glyph and covering every instance (a count still applies when it is drawn). Default 100: always drawn. A copy shape whose original was skipped has nothing to copy and is skipped too.

onlyForGlyphs.description: When set, this shape is drawn only in these glyphs (names from glyphs/baseGlyphs); null = every plain glyph. A copy of this shape is drawn only where this shape is.

excludeGlyphs.description: Glyphs this shape is never drawn in (applied after OnlyForGlyphs). Empty = none.

isDrawn.description: false: the shape is generated and placed like any other - it blocks other shapes, counts for crossing and spacing, and can be copied, derived and combined - but it is left out of the rendered glyph (and out of its framing). Use it as an invisible blockade or spacer. Shown only in the extra debug images, in their own colour, when render.debugShowUndrawn is on. Default true.

nodes.description: [x, y] points relative to the placement origin - Literal shapes only.

placement.description: Where the shape goes and how it is rotated.

arrangement.description: How the shape relates to the shapes already placed.

seedLabel.description: Advanced: prefix of this shape's random streams, which defaults to "shape-" plus the id. Only needed to make a migrated config reproduce its old glyphs exactly (the migration tool sets it); leave it out otherwise.

copyOf.description: Makes this entry a copy of an earlier shape instead of drawing it (see CopyConfig). Leave out kind, count, chain, nodes and placement on such an entry.

ShapeDefinition.description: One entry in a language's shapes list: a kind of stroke every plain glyph is built from. The list is processed in order, each entry placed against everything before it. Omit count for a guaranteed shape (exactly one, always present); give a count range for free-form strokes (rolled per glyph, and the only kind affected by usageSizeBias).

sides.description: Prefer only: one or two sides; two means a corner. Left with Right, or Top with Bottom, cancel out.

pick.description: SetRandom only: what is drawn. Default Any.

weight.description: How strongly the pull counts against the arrangement's bias, when both are active (default 1; 0 turns it off).

SidePull.description: Pulls a shape towards a side or corner of the glyph. Among the shape's legal placements (the best-of-N candidates of its arrangement) the one nearest the chosen side(s) is kept. A ranking only: it never relaxes a hard rule, and the pull is as strong as arrangement.candidates is high.

minCenterDistance.description: Minimum distance between the CENTROIDS of two shapes (the average of each shape's own node positions) - a coarse "keep this shape in its own area of the grid" check, independent of how close any individual pair of nodes gets.

minNodeDistance.description: Minimum distance between the CLOSEST pair of nodes belonging to two different shapes - a finer, local check that catches two shapes whose overall centers are far apart but which still reach out and nearly touch at one point.

maxNodeDistance.description: Maximum distance between the CLOSEST pair of nodes of the candidate and an existing shape. 0 = no maximum. Which existing shapes it must hold against is controlled by MaxDistanceMode. Must be >= MinNodeDistance when both are set.

ignoreStartNode.description: For a shape with placement.startOnExistingNode: leave the node it starts on out of the spacing checks (centroid, minimum and maximum node distance), since that node is shared with an existing shape and so sits at distance 0 from it. Every other node of the shape is still measured. Default false.

SpacingConfig.description: Spacing enforced between a shape and the shapes already placed, on top of (not instead of) the ordinary intersection check. Part of a shape's (or a combination's) arrangement rules; the spacing within one chain is ChainRules.SelfSpacing. Minimums keep things from sitting uncomfortably close together; maximums keep them clustered. Disabled by default, since these are additional constraints that can make placement noticeably harder to satisfy. A "shape" is one placed instance of a shapes entry when generating a glyph, and a whole placed component when combining glyphs per Combination.Recipes - both go through SubSymbolSpacingChecker. The rules of the shape BEING PLACED are checked against EVERY already-placed shape (minimums against all; the maximum per MaxDistanceMode), so the result depends on placement order.

range.description: Used only when Options is empty.

TensionConfig.description: Bezier handle length as a fraction of the edge's length (capped at 0.5 downstream). Default behavior (Options empty) is a single continuous range, uniformly sampled - the same as a plain FloatRange used to be. Populating Options switches to a weighted pick among several ranges instead: this is what lets a language express an extreme/bimodal distribution like "70% dead straight (0-0), 30% strongly curved (0.4-0.5)" rather than one smooth spread across the whole range - a look a single continuous range can't produce, since it always fills in the middle values too. Not restricted to two options; any number of weighted bands works, following the same {value/range, weight} pattern as ConnectionRuleConfig and ScaleFactorConfig elsewhere in this schema.

TensionOption.description: One weighted tension range to pick from - see TensionConfig.

width.description: Width along the body of the stroke.

flareLength.description: Flare length as a fraction of each edge's length (capped at 0.5).

ballScale.description: Ball diameter = EndWidth * BallScale (Terminal == Ball only).

perGlyphJitter.description: 0 = every glyph uses the identical typeface; 0.1 = each glyph's widths vary by up to +-10%.

TypefaceConfig.description: One typeface per language, resolved once from the seed (so every glyph in a language reads as the same font). Kind selects which sub-config is used; a null sub-config means defaults.

strength.description: Extra draws added per use. 0 = off.

UsageSizeBiasConfig.description: Counteracts a size skew towards heavily-used component glyphs: the more recipes a plain glyph appears in, the more likely it is to roll LOW values for its sub-symbol count and sub-symbol lengths. (Components used rarely are the ones regenerated most while composites are being fitted, and what survives that is biased towards smaller, easier-to-place shapes - so the untouched, frequently-used ones end up bigger on average.) Mechanism: each use adds Strength "extra draws" - the glyph rolls its count/length that many extra times (the usual range, the usual rules) and keeps the lowest result. A fractional number of extra draws is honoured probabilistically. The result is always inside the configured min..max, so this only reshapes the odds; it never overrides a range or any other constraint. "Uses" = how many times the glyph's name appears across Combination.Recipes. A glyph used in no recipe is unaffected, as is everything when Strength is 0 (the default), in which case generation is bit-for-bit what it was. Rough feel, for a 3-value range (e.g. 1..3) and a glyph used twice: Strength 0.5 = 1 extra draw (lowest value ~55% of the time instead of 33%), Strength 1 = 2 extra draws (~70%). Guaranteed motifs have their own length range and are not affected.
